sections.title: The Recorded Volumes
sections.content: There are two reports about a cup at noon. Report A says the cup held 70 mL. Report B says the cup held 90 mL. Because neither report has precedence, we have two different recorded volumes for the same object.

lesson.title: Understanding Quarters

sections.title: What is a Quarter?
sections.content: A quarter means four equal parts that make up a whole. When you have a group of items, one quarter is just one of those four equal parts.

sections.title: Example: Twelve Counters
sections.content: If you have twelve counters, one quarter is three counters. This is because 12 divided into four equal parts equals 3 (Section 1).

lesson.summary: A quarter is one of four equal parts of a whole. For example, three is a quarter of twelve.

lesson.title: Understanding One Quarter

sections.title: What is a Quarter?
sections.content: One quarter is one of four equal parts of a whole. This means if you take one whole thing and divide it into four pieces that are all the same size, each piece is one quarter.

sections.title: Example with Counters
sections.content:
We can see this using counters. If you have twelve counters in total, one quarter of those counters is three. 

Calculation: 12 divided into 4 equal parts = 3.

lesson.title: Cup Observations

sections.title: The First Observation
sections.content: At noon, the cup held 70 mL of liquid. This is the first measurement recorded in the text (Section: 1).

sections.title: The Second Observation
sections.content:
At one o'clock, the cup held 90 mL of liquid. The source states that 20 mL was added to the cup between noon and one o'clock (Section: 1). 

Calculation: 70 mL + 20 mL = 90 mL.

lesson.title: Understanding Halves

sections.title: What is a Half?
sections.content: A half is one of two equal groups. When you put these two equal groups together, they make the whole collection (Section 1).

sections.title: Example: Seeds
sections.content: Imagine a jar with eight seeds. If you split them into two equal groups, each group has four seeds. Therefore, half of eight seeds is four seeds (Section 1).

lesson.summary: A half is one of two equal parts that make up a whole. For example, half of eight seeds is four seeds.
objectives: Explain a half using simple words
